priority_actions.display_misconception: flips sign when reading a root from a bracket
priority_actions.why: 21 occurrences over 30 days on Quadratic equations — the pattern is persistent and not breaking with the current approach. Prior drills: 2 failed — switching approach.
priority_actions.instruction:
Switch from verbal rehearsal to comparative worked examples.
1. Show the learner two versions of the same question side by side:
   Version A — roots with signs flipped correctly from brackets.
   Version B — roots copied from brackets without flipping signs.
2. Ask: 'Which one matches the rule, and why?'
3. Have them attempt a fresh question using the version they chose as correct.
4. Do not verbalise the rule this time — the comparison teaches it.
priority_actions.escalation_reason: Two prior drill sessions, both failed. The current format is not reaching the misconception — switching to a different teaching approach.
priority_actions.learner_prompt: “Plus three in the bracket — minus three as the root.” (say the sign inside, then say the opposite as the root)
priority_actions.teacher_reinforcement: “That’s the habit. The sign inside lies — the root flips it.”
priority_actions.success_criterion: 3 consecutive questions on quadratic equations where the learner does NOT exhibit: flips sign when reading a root from a bracket

failure_branch.trigger: 3 failures in a row on this drill
failure_branch.next_action: next plan regeneration will switch approach
